Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

MFO (development version)

Breaking changes

  • MFO_db gains a first column Step: the step number in the test (0 = resting row with include_basal = TRUE). It identifies the resting row instead of Load == "basal". Code that selects MFO_db columns by position must be updated (SPEC 14).

  • MFO_db$Load is now the measured load of each step (numeric; NA for the resting row and when there is no load), no longer the synthetic label "basal", 15, 30, … of v0.1.0–0.2.1. This closes the known issue of 0.2.1 (SPEC 9.5, 14).

New features

  • MFO_protocol() describes the test (SPEC 14): "step" (fixed durations, as before), "step_variable" (a vector of durations whose last element is repeated, e.g. c(300, 180) for a 5-min first step; the averaged segment can also vary per step) and "relative" (steps in W/kg). It also records the load schedule (load_start, load_increment, load_unit) and the exercise mode. MFO() and MFOs() gain protocol = NULL; the default builds a "step" protocol from step_duration and steady_state_duration and gives the same results as 0.2.1. If both are supplied, protocol is used with a warning. MFO() returns protocol and mode; the MFOs() summary gains the columns protocol and mode.

  • Measured load (SPEC 14): an optional Load column of db_MFO (W or km/h) is averaged per step like VO2; without it the load schedule of the protocol (load_start + (Step - 1) * load_increment) is used, otherwise NA. MFO() returns Fatmax and the Fatmax zone in load units (FAT_MAX_load, FatMax_zone_lower_load, FatMax_zone_upper_load) by linear interpolation between steps, with load_unit and load_source ("file", "protocol", "none"). With MFO_protocol("relative") a Load column is divided by body_mass to give W/kg. MFOs() gains col_name_Load and the same columns. Example data: Fatmax 36.2 %VO2max = 86.5 W, zone 44.4–122.8 W.

  • VO2max_from_test() returns VO2max (highest 30-s rolling mean, as in MFO()) with maximality criteria: plateau (< 150 ml/min between the last two stages), peak RER > 1.10 and peak HR >= 90 % of the predicted HRmax (Tanaka 208 - 0.7 age by default, or Fox 220 - age; needs the new age argument). It is labelled "VO2max" with a plateau, or without one when RER and HR are both met, and "VO2peak" otherwise. Criteria after Howley, Bassett & Welch (1995), with the plateau threshold of Taylor et al.

    1. they report; HRmax equation of Tanaka, Monahan & Seals (2001). The Fox equation (220 - age) as the one in common use described by Tanaka et al. The RER and HR thresholds are pending source verification. Thresholds are arguments (SPEC 14, 19). MFO() and MFOs() gain age and return VO2max_type (and MFO() VO2max_criteria); VO2max also accepts a VO2max_from_test() result. Without age, MFO() says once per session that the HR criterion was not evaluated.

  • MFO_bayes() fits the SIN model in g/min (or a P3) as a Bayesian model with brms on Stan (SPEC 13.2; brms and rstan in Suggests) and returns posterior medians and credible intervals of MFO, Fatmax, Fatmin, the Fatmax zone, d, s and t, the contraction of each quantity (labelled prior-dominated below 0.5), the largest posterior correlation among d, s and t, and the sampler diagnostics. The SIN is parametrised by MFO, Fatmax, Fatmin and s, with d and t from the closed forms of Fatmax and Fatmin; priors Fatmax ~ N(50, 15) on (10, 90), Fatmin ~ N(90, 14) on (Fatmax, 100), s ~ LogNormal(0, 0.3) and MFO ~ N(0.45, 0.25) above 0. The priors first proposed in SPEC 13.2, on d, s and t, covered the true s in 7-10 % of simulated tests where t is far from 0. sigma = "proportional" lets the error grow with intensity; adapt_delta = 0.99 by default. Known limitation: Fatmax is underestimated by a median of 1.1-1.6 %VO2max in simulated tests (smaller than the 1.6-5.0 %VO2max typical error of the classical fits); a wider prior of s reduces it but causes divergent transitions. MFO_prior_check() draws the curves implied by the priors. It does not replace MFO() and is not part of MFOs(). New vignette vignette("bayes").

  • MFO_kinetics() gains fit = c("normalised", "absolute") (SPEC 13.2). "absolute" fits fat oxidation in g/min with MFO as a fourth parameter (MFO_SIN), so it has no bias from normalising by the highest observed step: in noiseless simulated tests it recovered d, s, t, Fatmax, Fatmin and MFO to 1e-6 with Fatmax between steps, where the normalised fit gave d = 0.234 instead of 0.18. With noise it removes most of the bias of d and Fatmin but not their spread, and it improves MFO in bias and precision; d is poorly identified with noisy data (inst/validation/sin_noise.R). The default stays "normalised" (Chenevière et al. 2009) and is to be reviewed at 0.3.0-beta.1. MFO_kinetics() also gains ci, B, conf and seed (intervals for d, s, t, Fatmax, Fatmin and MFO_SIN; leverage from the gradient of the fit for the bootstrap). MFOs() gains sin_fit and sin_ci (default FALSE: the SIN interval is opt-in, as it doubles the run time) and reports MFO_SIN, FatMax_SIN_lower/upper and Fatmin_lower/upper. ?MFO_kinetics now says that d, s and t are not interpreted one by one with real data; Fatmax, Fatmin and MFO are.

  • MFO() and MFOs() gain ci = c("none", "bootstrap"), B (2000), conf (0.95) and seed (SPEC 13.1). With "bootstrap", the fit is repeated on fitted values plus resampled modified residuals, r / sqrt(1 - h), centred (Davison & Hinkley 1997), and percentile intervals are returned for MFO, Fatmax, the Fatmax zone and Fatmax in load units (ci, bootstrap); MFOs() reports MFO_lower, MFO_upper, FAT_MAX_lower and FAT_MAX_upper. Available for P3, P2 and MRER (its two regressions resampled separately), not for MV. With show_ci = TRUE (default) the plot shows the interval in the subtitle and Fatmax’s as a grey band. It is the uncertainty of the fit within one test; it assumes exchangeable residuals. The default "none" leaves results and run time unchanged. ci = "parametric" (also ci = TRUE, the recommended interval) draws sigma^2 ~ Inv-chi^2(n - p, s^2) for each replicate and then normal errors: the posterior of normal regression with a flat prior (Gelman et al. 2013), which carries the uncertainty of sigma. In the ideal case (P2 on a parabola, 8 steps, normal errors, 500 tests) it covered Fatmax 94.4 % and MFO 95.4 %, against 88.2 % and 89.2 % for the residual bootstrap. A P2 vertex outside the measured intensities now warns and flags the interval. ?MFO documents that MRER overestimates Fatmax (+3-4 %VO2max) against SIN curves, so its interval rarely covers the truth. The coverage study is in vignette("validation") and inst/validation/bootstrap_coverage.R.

  • MFO_reliability() computes the test-retest reliability of the MFOs() outcomes from two or more sessions per participant (SPEC 12): ICC(2,1) with the F-based confidence interval of McGraw & Wong (1996, corrected), classified by its lower bound (Koo & Li 2016); SEM, MDC95 and MDC90 (Weir 2005); CV = SEM/mean and the log-scale CV of Hopkins (2000) for all variables; bias with its confidence interval and limits of agreement (Bland & Altman 1986) for each pair of consecutive sessions, with a heteroscedasticity check; and, with three sessions or more, a familiarization check of session 1 (p < 0.05 and a difference larger than the SEM). Participants and sessions come from columns, the sessions.csv of write_MFO_sessions() or the ID split at its last underscore. plot() draws Bland-Altman plots. The ICC and its interval equal psych::ICC (ICC2) to 1e-10; psych is in Suggests for that test.

  • simulate_MFO_sessions() generates repeated MFO tests (resting, MFO and graded tables ready for MFO()) for several participants and sessions with a known truth (SPEC 12, 13). Fat oxidation follows the SIN model (shape = "basic", "trained" from Chenevière et al. 2009, Fig. 5, or d and s per participant) and VCO2 inverts the chosen author equation, so without noise MFO() and MFO_kinetics() recover MFO, Fatmax, d, s, t and Fatmin (exactly when a step falls on Fatmax). Variability: between participants (MFO and Fatmax defaults of Amaro-Gahete et al. 2018; VO2max must be given), between sessions (cv_MFO 0.21 and cv_Fatmax 0.26, the total test-retest CVs of Chrzanowski-Smith et al. 2020, an upper bound when used as day-to-day variation), familiarization of session 1, and analyser noise per record (noise_cv, noise_cor, 0 by default, with no recommended value). write_MFO_sessions() writes the sessions as folders for MFOs() and a sessions.csv mapping each folder to its participant and session. fat_noise_cv adds to each step an error of SD fat_noise_cv x MFO around the true curve, the noise definition of SPEC 17; the gas noise (noise_cv, noise_cor) stays as an option, with no realistic value for the correlation.

  • read_cart() reads a metabolic cart export (Cortex, Cosmed, Vyntus or ZAN, parsed by the spiro package, now in Suggests) and returns the tables MFO() expects in the internal data contract (SPEC 16): Time, VO2, VCO2 (mL/min), RER and, when present, HR, Load, VE. Breaths are averaged in fixed intervals (10 s by default; empty intervals are kept as NA so records stay aligned); VO2 above a median of 100 is read as mL/min and below it the unit must be given (vo2_unit, with body_mass for mL/kg/min); RER is recomputed as VCO2/VO2 and an exported RER off by more than 0.02 is counted with a warning; phases are split by the user’s cuts (basal_end, MFO_end). No personal data from the file are kept. None of the devices has yet been validated with a real export of MFO’s own.

  • The example data MFO_df gain a Load column (25–200 W, 25-W stages), as described in their documentation.

  • MFO_protocol() gains "ramp" and "single_day" (SPEC 14). A ramp is read as windows of ramp_window s (30 by default, rounded up to whole records), one every ramp_step s (back to back by default); min_steps counts non-overlapping windows, method = "MV" stops with an error suggesting P3, and a load schedule is load_start plus load_increment per minute at each window midpoint (ramp vs. graded protocols, Physiologia 2025, Teso et al.). A single-day test has cut_time: records after it are the graded test, used for VO2max when db_graded and VO2max are not given (Sports Med Health Sci 2026, Marín-Galindo et al.). Automatic detection of the phases is left to the importers (SPEC 16).

Bug fixes

  • method = "P2" returned the vertex of the parabola as Fatmax even when its curvature was positive, i.e. a minimum of fat oxidation (#38; affects 0.2.1 and earlier). Without a maximum (curvature >= 0 or NA coefficients) P2 now uses the highest observed step (MV) with a warning, as MRER does. New method_used in MFO() (and the MFOs() summary) reports the method actually used after any fallback (P3 to P2, P2 or MRER to MV); method is still the one requested, and the plot shows both when they differ.

  • VO2max_from_test() (new in 0.3.0-alpha.1) compared the last two runs of equal Load, so a recovery or a rest pause at the end of the graded test was taken as the final stage and a falling VO2 counted as a plateau. The final stage is now the last one at the highest load and the previous stage is the one before it with load > 0. With the ZAN example of spiro the plateau goes from -1831 ml/min (met) to +1655 ml/min (not met); the example data of MFO are unchanged (+247 ml/min) (SPEC 14).

  • MFOs() treated every entry of path as a participant: a stray file (e.g. a note) gave an error row. It now reads only folders with from = "folder" and only .xlsx files with from = "files".

  • use_incomplete_step = TRUE averaged only the last record of the incomplete step instead of its last steady_state_duration s, as documented (the start was counted from the nominal end of the step). In the example data cut to 66 records, step 8 VO2 goes from 2495 (one record) to 2444.7 ml/min (last 60 s). The default (FALSE) is not affected (#26, SPEC 9.5).

Documentation

  • New vignette “Validation of the confidence intervals” (vignette("validation")): coverage of the intervals of MFO(ci = ) by method, number of steps and noise on simulated tests with a SIN truth, with the model bias of each method. Results computed once with inst/validation/bootstrap_coverage.R and written into the article.

  • Vignette: new section “Protocols, load and VO2max” (protocol types, Fatmax in watts, VO2max vs VO2peak, ramps and single-day tests); the generated methods paragraph reports Fatmax in W.

MFO 0.2.1

CRAN release: 2026-11-12

First CRAN release since 0.1.0 (2022). Scientific background and sources of every formula in docs/SPEC.md (GitHub repository).

Breaking changes

  • method = "MRER" now implements the MRER of Chenevière et al. (2009, p. 1617): (1 − RER) and VO2 are fitted as straight lines of %VO2max and Fatmax is the vertex of their product, 1.7 (1 − RER) VO2. In v0.2.0, "MRER" was a different method: it returned the step with the highest observed 1.7 (1 − RER) VO2, a measured-values (MV) method. That behaviour is now method = "MV", which uses the author equation (same step; MFO differs by the ratio of coefficients, e.g. 1.67/1.7 with Frayn). In the example data (Frayn) "MRER" moves from Fatmax 41.0 %VO2max / MFO 0.339 g/min to 35.8 %VO2max / 0.327 g/min; "MV" gives 41.0 %VO2max / 0.327 g/min (SPEC 6.1, 19 finding 4).

  • Results change with the default arguments. Because 0.2.0 never reached CRAN, users updating from 0.1.0 also get the 0.2.0 changes listed below (default method = "P3" instead of a second-degree polynomial). In 0.2.1: VO2max is a 30-s rolling mean, so Fatmax, the Fatmax zone and the crossover point (%VO2max) increase; the SIN parameters d and t follow Chenevière et al. (2009) and are not comparable with earlier values; Fatmin is the second zero of the SIN curve; "Peronnet" coefficients change in the 4th decimal; resting values use the author equation. See Bug fixes for the size of each change and how to reproduce 0.2.0.

New features

  • method = "MV" (measured values) in MFO() and MFOs(): Fatmax is the step with the highest observed FAT. R_squared and RMSE are NA; the Fatmax zone uses linear interpolation between steps and is labelled so in the plot and in the new FatMax_zone_method element (SPEC 6.1).

  • MFO() and MFOs() gain include_basal (default FALSE). With TRUE the resting row enters MFO_db as step 0 and is part of the P3/P2 fit, as in Montes de Oca et al. (2021). The default reproduces v0.1.0/v0.2.0, which silently lost the resting row because its HR is NA; the exclusion is now explicit and no longer depends on missing HR. Example data, Frayn, P3: MFO 0.3167 -> 0.3225 g/min and Fatmax 36.17 -> 36.11 %VO2max with TRUE (SPEC 9.5).

  • RER_cutoff accepts names from Amaro-Gahete et al. (2019): "classic" = 1.00, "safe" = 0.95, "sedentary" = 0.93, "trained" = 0.90. Numbers still work. Example data (Frayn, P3): 7, 6, 5 and 4 of 8 steps kept; Fatmax 33.9, 35.7, 36.9 and 29.5 %VO2max (SPEC 19, finding 2).

  • energy_equivalents argument in MFO() and MFOs() for Kcal and x_Kcal: "classic" (4 kcal/g CHO, 9 kcal/g FAT, default in 0.2.x, as in v0.2.0) or "source": Péronnet & Massicotte (1991, Table 1) 3.8683/9.7460 kcal/g for "Peronnet" and, as a package decision, "Frayn" (Frayn 1983 gives none); Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5) CHO 3.95 kcal/g below 50 %VO2max and 4.07 at or above, fat 9.75 kcal/g, for "Jeukendrup" (resting row: Péronnet & Massicotte values). MFO and Fatmax are not affected. In the example data (Frayn) "source" changes step Kcal by −1.9 % to +5.3 %. The default will change to "source" in 0.3.0; when the argument is not set, a message says so once per session (SPEC 19, finding 1).

  • MFO_kinetics() and MFOs() gain fatmin_threshold (default NULL, Fatmin at the second zero of the SIN curve); a proportion of MFO such as 0.05 gives the intensity above Fatmax where fat oxidation falls to that fraction, in closed form. The kinetics plot now shows the observed steps and draws the fitted curve between its two zeros (SPEC 19, finding 3).

  • Quality warnings in MFO() and MFOs() (new section Quality warnings in ?MFO): new argument min_steps (default 6) warns when fewer exercise steps enter the fit after RER_cutoff and negative_FAT = "exclude" (the resting row does not count); and a warning when Fatmax is at the edge, i.e. the exercise step nearest to Fatmax is the first or the last one (the test may have started too high or stopped too early). Results are unchanged. The example data give neither warning; with RER_cutoff = "sedentary" (5 steps) min_steps warns, and with "trained" (4 steps) MV, MRER and P2 also put Fatmax at the last step (SPEC 14).

  • Incomplete last step: records left after the last complete step now always give a warning (“Last step incomplete (120 s of 180 s)”); v0.2.0 dropped them silently. The new use_incomplete_step argument of MFO() and MFOs() (default FALSE, results as in v0.2.0) uses that step only if it lasts at least steady_state_duration, averaging its last steady_state_duration s (SPEC 9.5).

  • MFOs() re-issues every warning with the participant ID first ("P02: No HR data in db_MFO: ..."), so the quality warnings can be traced in a batch. The summary gains FatMax_zone_method and energy_equivalents, and MFO() returns energy_equivalents.

  • MFO() returns VO2max, VO2max_window (effective, s) and VO2max_window_requested; MFOs() gains vo2max_window and the columns VO2max and VO2max_window.

Bug fixes

  • SIN model: MFO_kinetics() now implements equation [14] of Chenevière et al. (2009), pi^(1/s) / (pi + 2*d); v0.1.0/v0.2.0 computed pi^(1/s) / pi + 2*d. Both describe the same family of curves, so the fitted curve can be the same, but d and t take different values: the old d was not Chenevière’s dilatation and is not comparable with published values. With their Fig. 5 parameters (d = 0.18, s = 1.52, t = 0.21) the old formula put Fatmax at 28.9 %VO2max instead of 58.2 (SPEC 6.5, 19 finding 5).

  • SIN fitting procedure: MFO_kinetics() now fits the model directly to the observed steps (%MFO normalised to the highest observed step), as Chenevière et al. (2009) did. v0.1.0/v0.2.0 fitted a grid of ≥ 50 points predicted by a third-degree polynomial, which inflated n and shrank the standard errors of d, s and t. FatMax_SIN and Fatmin now come from closed forms derived from eq. [14], and Fatmin is the second zero of the curve, (π + d − t)/K, instead of the first grid point below 5 % of MFO. Example data (Frayn): d 0.144 -> −0.385, s 0.935 -> 0.910, t −0.093 -> 0.355, FatMax_SIN 36.0 -> 36.2, Fatmin 76.0 -> 76.4 %VO2max, R² 0.997 -> 0.965 (now on the observed steps); standard errors grow 20–60 fold to their honest size. With negative_FAT = "exclude" or RER_cutoff = 1 (Chenevière’s step selection) the example gives s = 0.54 and Fatmin = 85.3 %VO2max: the SIN is sensitive to the last step, see ?MFO_kinetics (SPEC 6.5, 19 findings 3 and 7).

  • MFO_kinetics() now distinguishes two warnings: with fewer than 4 steps the SIN cannot be fitted (convergence = FALSE, as before); with 4 or 5 steps it is fitted but warns that the fit is unreliable and that at least 6 steps are recommended (SPEC 6.5).

  • VO2max from db_graded is now the highest rolling mean over the new vo2max_window argument (default 30 s) instead of the single highest record. If the window is not a multiple of step_time, the number of records is rounded up (30 s with 20-s records = 2 records = 40 s) and a message reports the effective window. Fatmax, the Fatmax zone and the crossover point (%VO2max) increase by the ratio old/new VO2max; MFO (g/min) is unchanged. In the example data VO2max drops from 3442 to 3315 ml/min and Fatmax moves from 34.8 to 36.2 %VO2max. Use vo2max_window = step_time to reproduce v0.2.0 (SPEC 9.5, 14).

  • Resting substrate oxidation (x_CHO, x_FAT, x_Kcal) now uses the same author equations as the test; it always used Frayn before. Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005) propose no resting equation: with author = "Jeukendrup" the package uses the 100 % glucose pair derived from their Table 4 constants (CHO = 4.58519 VCO2 − 3.22597 VO2, FAT = 1.69469 VO2 − 1.70130 VCO2), documented as a package decision. MFO and Fatmax are not affected because the resting row is not part of the fit. Example data with "Peronnet": resting CHO 0.130 -> 0.134 g/min, FAT 0.0726 -> 0.0723 g/min (SPEC 9.5).

  • Péronnet & Massicotte (1991) print no oxidation equations: "Peronnet" now derives them in code from the O2/CO2 constants of their Table 1 (glucose 0.7455/0.7426, fatty acid 2.0092/1.4136 L/g): CHO = 4.58519 VCO2 − 3.22597 VO2, FAT = 1.69469 VO2 − 1.70130 VCO2, instead of the rounded 4.585/3.2255/1.6946/1.7012. Changes are in the 4th decimal: example data, Fatmax 35.288 -> 35.285 %VO2max, MFO unchanged at 0.3158 g/min, resting CHO 0.13369 -> 0.13361 g/min. Frayn (1983) prints his equations, which stay as printed (4.55/3.21; 1.67/1.67); their derivation from his Table 1 is a cross-check test (SPEC 19, finding 6).

  • With author = "Jeukendrup", MFO() now warns once when exercise steps fall outside 40–75 %VO2max, the range of the Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5) equations, and lists their intensities; those steps were extrapolated silently before. Steps removed by RER_cutoff and the resting row never warn. Values are unchanged (SPEC 3, 9.5).

  • Heart rate never decides which rows or steps are dropped. In v0.2.0 a test without an HR column made MFO() fail (0 (non-NA) cases; in MFOs() an empty row with no explanation), a step without HR was silently removed from the fit, and read_MFO_databases() deleted every row with a missing HR value, shifting all later steps (an empty HR column deleted the whole table). Now only VO2, VCO2 and RER remove rows, MFO and Fatmax are computed as usual, and a warning says that FAT_MAX_HR and FAT_MAX_porcHRmax are NA (no HR) or interpolated from fewer steps (some steps without HR, listed by %VO2max) (SPEC 9.5).

  • When both VO2max and db_graded are given, VO2max is now used and db_graded is ignored with a warning (v0.2.0 silently used db_graded).

  • Plots no longer cover the curves with text. MFO_plot shows FATmax, MFO and the method in the subtitle, explains the Fatmax zone and the crossover point in the caption, and has a FAT/CHO legend; MFO_kinetics_plot shows d, s, t, Fatmin and R² in the subtitle. Values are unchanged.

  • substrate_oxidation() no longer fails on vectors with author = "Jeukendrup"; each value picks its own equation.

Documentation

  • New vignette “From gas exchange to Fatmax” (vignette("mfo-workflow")): each step of MFO() rebuilt by hand and checked against the package, the four methods compared, the SIN model and its sensitivity to negative_FAT, the effect of RER_cutoff and include_basal, a generated methods paragraph, and batch processing with MFOs().

  • pkgdown reference grouped by workflow; the vignette is the “Get started” article.

  • README rewritten for v0.2.x and generated from an executable README.Rmd.

  • Coefficients printed in the source are used as printed and cited by table or equation; derived coefficients are used only where the source prints no equation, with the derivation explained in the documentation (SPEC 19). Exercise equations of Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5) and Frayn (1983) are used as printed; their derivation from the published O2/CO2 constants is kept as a cross-check test.

  • Fixed the DOI of Achten et al. (2002) in DESCRIPTION.

  • GitHub Actions: R CMD check on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu (R devel, release, oldrel-1), test coverage with Codecov, and a pkgdown site deployed to https://jorgedelro.github.io/MFO/.

  • Tests for MFOs() in both modes ("folder" and "files"), checked against MFO() participant by participant; coverage of R/MFOs.R goes from 0 to 99 %.

Known issues (planned for 0.3.0)

  • MFO_db$Load is a synthetic step index (step * step_duration / 60 * 5), not measured load, and Fatmax is not returned in external-load units (W, km/h). A measured Load column is planned (SPEC 9.5, 14).

  • The SIN model is normalised to the highest observed step, so a noisy step rescales the whole curve; normalising to the fitted MFO will be evaluated (SPEC 9.5).

  • No confidence intervals for MFO, Fatmax or Fatmin yet (SPEC 13).

  • The default of energy_equivalents will change from "classic" to "source".

MFO 0.2.0

GitHub release (February 2026). Not submitted to CRAN.

New features

  • MFO() gains method to choose the curve-fitting method: "P3" (third-degree polynomial, new default), "P2" and "MRER". Version 0.1.0 always used a second-degree polynomial.
  • MFO() gains author = "Peronnet" (Péronnet & Massicotte, 1991) in addition to "Frayn" and "Jeukendrup".
  • New protocol arguments in MFO() and MFOs(): step_duration (default 180 s) and steady_state_duration (default 60 s).
  • New artefact handling: RER_cutoff removes steps above an RER threshold; negative_FAT chooses whether negative fat oxidation is truncated to 0, excluded or kept.
  • New outputs in MFO(): Fatmax zone (fat oxidation within 10 % of MFO), crossover point, heart rate at Fatmax and Fatmax as %HRmax (HRmax), MFO relative to body mass (body_mass) and to fat-free mass (fat_free_mass), and R_squared / RMSE of the fit.
  • MFO_kinetics() now returns standard errors of d, s and t, FatMax_SIN, Fatmin, R_squared, RMSE and a convergence flag, and handles fitting failures without stopping.
  • MFOs() passes all new MFO() arguments through and gains output_format ("xlsx", "csv" or "rds").
  • Internal helper to average breath-by-breath data into fixed intervals.

Other changes

  • Requires R >= 4.1.0 (was R >= 2.10).
  • Expanded unit tests.

MFO 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2022-02-11

First CRAN release (February 2022).

  • MFO() computes MFO and Fatmax from resting, incremental and maximal test data, with Frayn (1983) or Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005) equations and a second-degree polynomial fit.
  • MFO_kinetics() fits the SIN model of Cheneviere et al. (2009) and returns dilatation, symmetry and translation.
  • MFOs() processes a folder of participants.
